title: Part E · A real connected-store workflow
narration: This is Part E of the Google ADK assignment, implemented with PostgreSQL, MCP Toolbox, Vertex AI and Shopify. The user approved replacing AlloyDB after the cloud trial was unavailable. This walkthrough shows actual code and saved live execution evidence. The application fetched fifteen products and twenty four variants from the authorized Shopify store. Some product names resemble Shopify demonstration inventory, so this is a connected store demonstration, not proof of a production merchant catalog. No product rows or provider responses were fabricated by this application. The database runs locally, and Gemini still uses Vertex AI through Application Default Credentials.

title: 01 · Import once, synchronize safely
narration: The catalog importer creates a PostgreSQL connection, starts a transaction, and acquires a per merchant advisory lock. It then fetches the complete Shopify catalog before writing a new synchronization record. Each product and variant retains its original Shopify identifier. Upserts update existing records rather than creating duplicates. After a complete fetch, records absent from the new snapshot become inactive. A failed or incomplete fetch rolls back the transaction. Prices, availability and images come from Shopify. The database includes a generated full text search document and a GIN index. Search is explicitly lexical; the project does not pretend to have semantic embeddings.

title: 02 · MCP tools and Vertex orchestration
narration: The ADK agent connects to MCP Toolbox using its real Streamable HTTP transport. Its tool filter exposes only search catalog and get product details. The Toolbox configuration uses fixed SQL with bound parameters. A separate database reader role can select product and variant rows but cannot access users or modify products. Gemini is explicitly configured for Vertex with the user's project and location. The server records tool names from actual ADK events. Authenticated requests can also read their own cart and refresh Shopify availability through closures carrying the verified subject. The chat model has no cart mutation tool. Purchase-related changes remain behind explicit interface confirmations.

title: 03 · Ownership is enforced server-side
narration: Local accounts use independently generated bearer credentials. The database stores only their hashes, and the browser holds the credential in memory until sign out. This is local account authentication, not Google OAuth. Cart lookups always constrain the local cart identifier, the authenticated subject, and the merchant. A prompt or request body cannot choose another user identity. Shopify's secret cart identifier stays on the server. The application role is separate from the migration owner, and ADK session tables use a dedicated schema. Public production hosting would require additional identity lifecycle, HTTPS, managed secrets, monitoring and operational controls. This delivery intentionally remains loopback only.

title: 04 · Confirmed and duplicate-safe cart actions
narration: Every cart mutation requires a true confirmation flag and a request UUID. The service hashes the payload, locks the user's action stream, and persists an intent before contacting Shopify. If the same request identifier is repeated with the same payload, a completed result is returned without repeating the mutation. Reusing the identifier for different data is rejected. Shopify mutations are not automatically retried. If the result is uncertain after a network failure, the operation requires reconciliation. This prevents a blind retry from duplicating an action. Before adding items and producing a checkout handoff, the service reads live availability. Exact stock counts are unavailable with the current token's scopes.

title: 05 · Evidence, limitations and execution
narration: The recorded live check verifies actual PostgreSQL rows, an MCP search result, confirmed cart creation, idempotent add operations and cross user read and write denial. Shopify returned a genuine HTTPS checkout URL. The test removed its item afterward and never attempted payment. The Vertex agent called both catalog tools and returned an answer. Seventeen pure contract tests also pass. Order history is explicitly blocked because customer account authorization has not been configured. The following browser recording shows the actual local storefront, catalog search, confirmed cart action, checkout link and cleanup. It is an automated execution recording. This narration is synthesized, and no YouTube upload is claimed.
